newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds end mostly weaker amid new supply.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds end mostly weaker amid new supply.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed mostly weaker in quiet trade on Wednesday, underperforming U.S. issues, with new Canadian two- and 30-year supply weighing on prices, analysts said.

"The market started to break just as that (Quebec) issue was coming out and I think that kept pressure on the market over the course of the day," said Joe Lee, a portfolio manager with Laketon Investment Management.
Canada's 30-year benchmark fell C$0.22 to C$114.26 to yield 6.871 percent.

The U.S. 30-year bond rose 6/32 to yield 6.83 percent. The spread between the bonds widened to four basis points from an all-time low of one basis point at Tuesday's close. The Canada-U.S. 30-year spread had narrowed to zero during the course of yesterday's trading.
"I think there could have been some selling that came out into our market versus the U.S. because of the spread being so close in the long end," said Lee.
However, supply was the primary concern for the Canadian market analysts said, with both Quebec and Canada bringing issues to the market.
The province of Quebec this morning set C$350 million of 8.5 percent bonds due April 1, 2026 in financial markets, said lead manager Levesque Beaubien Geoffrion.
The bond was priced at C$114.843 to yield 7.262 percent, 40 basis points over the Government of Canada's 8.0 percent bond due June, 2023.

The Government of Canada also auctioned C$3.5 billion auction of its new 4.75 percent bonds due September 15, 1999. The auction produced an average yield of 4.823 percent and price of 99.853. Analysts said the auction attracted decent demand.

Analysts said investors are looking ahead to the release of U.S. retail sales and producer price reports on Thursday and Friday. Beyond that traders are focused on the July 1 meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee.

In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond traded unchanged at C$106.49 to yield 6.359 percent while the U.S. 10-year rose 2/32 to 6.56 percent.The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to 20 basis points from 21 basis points at Tuesday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 2.92 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 4.97 percent.
